title: The Unofficial Semester
premise: At Hollowmere Academy, every senior class 'inherits' the Founders' Keys — relics said to keep the town's dying mill economy alive through an old endowment ritual. When Beatrix Okonkwo's best friend Priya vanishes days before the Inheritance Ceremony, leaving behind a stolen key ring, Bea discovers the tradition is a laundering scheme run by the academy's trustees, and that students who ask questions are quietly erased from records. Following Priya's trail through sealed dormitory wings and the flooded mill beneath campus, Bea learns her own scholarship was funded by the same trust that disappeared her father fifteen years ago. In the end, Bea exposes the trustees during the ceremony itself, trades the final key for Priya's release, and chooses to rebuild the tradition into something honest rather than destroy the town that depends on it.
about_author: E. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former boarding school archivist who spent six years cataloguing the secrets of New England preparatory academies before turning to fiction. They write stories about careful kids who learn that survival and truth are not always the same thing.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Being Careful
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Establishes Hollowmere Academy, Bea's scholarship, her meticulous routines, and her fierce friendship with reckless Priya Chandra. Emotional beat: the exhausting safety of a life built to avoid attention.

chapters.title: The Keys on the Windowsill
chapters.summary: Bea finds Priya missing and a heavy antique key ring on their shared windowsill, tagged with a note: 'Don't turn them. Find me.' Emotional beat: fear disguised as calm.

chapters.title: Missing Persons, Missing Paperwork
chapters.summary: Bea reports Priya missing; the dean insists Priya 'withdrew' and produces a signature Bea knows is forged. POV alternates to Priya in a locked infirmary wing. Emotional beat: gaslighting meets resolve.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Ceremony
chapters.summary: Bea learns of the senior tradition: each class receives the Founders' Keys to 'renew the town's fortune.' Headmaster Voss watches her too closely. Emotional beat: dread dressed in pageantry.

chapters.title: First Key: The Chapel Basement
chapters.summary: Bea tests the smallest key and opens a chapel basement archive, finding decades of student records with names redacted — including her father's. Emotional beat: the past reaching up to grab her.

chapters.title: An Ally with a Camera
chapters.summary: Bea reluctantly recruits Marcus, Priya's ex and the school paper's photographer, who has been documenting trustee meetings. Emotional beat: mistrust becoming fragile alliance.

chapters.title: The Trust That Paid for Me
chapters.summary: Bea traces her scholarship to the Hollowmere Founders' Trust — the same entity that employed her father before his 'accident.' Emotional beat: grief reframed as evidence.

chapters.title: Redacted
chapters.summary: Bea and Marcus find seven students across fifty years who vanished mid-semester, all scholarship kids, all erased. Emotional beat: horror in a filing cabinet.

chapters.title: Priya's Voice Mail
chapters.summary: A delayed voice mail from Priya surfaces: 'The keys are real, Bea. The mill is real. Don't let them do the renewal without me.' Emotional beat: hope with a countdown attached.

chapters.title: The Flooded Mill
chapters.summary: Following a map hidden in Priya's notebook, Bea reaches the sealed mill beneath campus and finds the 'endowment' is a vault of trust documents — and signs of recent habitation. Emotional beat: awe tipping into terror.

chapters.title: Voss Offers Her Everything
chapters.summary: Headmaster Voss privately offers Bea a full ride to any college, implying the price is silence. Emotional beat: temptation measured against loyalty.

chapters.title: What Priya Knew
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Priya's POV, three weeks earlier: Priya discovered the trust skims the town's pension funds and confronted a trustee. Emotional beat: bravery that cost everything.

chapters.title: The Second Key Turns
chapters.summary: Bea uses a second key on the dormitory's sealed fourth floor and finds Priya's belongings staged to look like a voluntary departure. Emotional beat: fury sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Marcus Gets a Warning
chapters.summary: Marcus's camera is stolen and a dead bird is left in his locker. He nearly quits; Bea admits she's scared too. Emotional beat: solidarity in the teeth of intimidation.

chapters.title: The Trustee Dinner
chapters.summary: Bea infiltrates a trustee dinner as a student server and overhears the 'renewal' scheduled for ceremony night — with a new name on the erasure list: hers. Emotional beat: icy clarity.

chapters.title: Her Father's File
chapters.summary: Bea reads her father's redacted file: he was the trust's accountant who found the skim, and his death was ruled an accident within a week. Emotional beat: inherited grief becoming inherited duty.

chapters.title: The Third Key and the Locked Girl
chapters.summary: A third key opens an old sanatorium annex where Bea finds signs Priya was held — and a current student, quiet Wren, who has been 'kept' there for months. Emotional beat: the scale of the machine revealed.

chapters.title: Wren's Silence
chapters.summary: Wren, terrified, reveals the trustees use 'withdrawals' to silence students who find the vault. She begs Bea to stop looking. Emotional beat: compassion versus self-preservation.

chapters.title: Counting the Days
chapters.summary: Bea maps the ceremony timeline: six days. She and Marcus plan to copy the vault documents, but need someone inside the administration. Emotional beat: the ticking clock made physical.

chapters.title: Ms. Achebe's Office
chapters.summary: Bea tests the school nurse-archivist, Ms. Achebe, who quietly reveals she's been misfiling records for years to protect students — and offers to help. Emotional beat: unexpected adult allyship.

chapters.title: The Fourth Key Fails
chapters.summary: The fourth key doesn't fit its lock — Priya swapped it, leaving a riddle in her notebook that points to the town's founding families. Emotional beat: a puzzle as a love letter.

chapters.title: Into Hollowmere Town
chapters.summary: Bea visits the dying mill town, meets retirees whose pensions are vanishing, and understands the tradition's human cost. Emotional beat: the stakes widening beyond school walls.

chapters.title: The Founder's Descendant
chapters.summary: Bea tracks the last founding-family descendant, elderly Ada Hollowmere, who confirms the keys open the trust vault — and that she's been paid to look away for decades. Emotional beat: complicity and shame across generations.

chapters.title: They Search Her Room
chapters.summary: Bea's room is ransacked; the key ring is gone, taken by Voss's aide. Marcus blames himself. Emotional beat: setback and the temptation to run.

chapters.title: The Fifth Key in the Organ
chapters.summary: Bea deduces Priya hid the real fifth key inside the chapel organ, where they sang together. Inside is also Priya's full evidence ledger. Emotional beat: friendship as a hiding place.

chapters.title: Ceremony Eve
chapters.summary: Rehearsal for the Inheritance Ceremony; Bea is unexpectedly named a key-bearer, placing her inside the ritual. Voss smiles at her. Emotional beat: being handed the trap as an honor.

chapters.title: Wren Disappears
chapters.summary: Wren is moved the night before she agreed to testify. Bea realizes the trustees are accelerating. Emotional beat: guilt and the cost of waiting.

chapters.title: The Plan on Paper
chapters.summary: Bea, Marcus, and Ms. Achebe finalize the plan: swap the ceremony's ceremonial keys with the real ones, open the vault publicly, and livestream the documents. Emotional beat: fear converted into choreography.

chapters.title: The Sixth Key
chapters.summary: Bea decodes the riddle's final line: the sixth key is 'held by the one who owes you.' It's been in Ms. Achebe's possession since Priya slipped it to her. Emotional beat: trust vindicated.

chapters.title: What Bea Is Willing to Lose
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude: Bea writes her father a letter she'll never send and accepts she may be expelled, erased, or worse. Emotional beat: the price of survival named out loud.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Ceremony
chapters.summary: The ceremony begins; Voss presents the keys, the trustees convene at the vault, and Bea — in ceremonial white — makes the swap under the town's watching eyes. Emotional beat: terror performed as poise.

chapters.title: The Vault Opens
chapters.summary: The real keys turn; the vault floods the ceremony hall with light and paper. Bea reads the skim aloud as Marcus streams it. Emotional beat: the moment silence breaks.

chapters.title: Voss Closes the Doors
chapters.summary: Voss locks the hall and offers Bea one last deal: her father's name cleared in exchange for the ledger. Bea refuses. Emotional beat: the temptation's final, cruelest form.

chapters.title: Priya, Found
chapters.summary: Following the trustees' panic, Ms. Achebe locates Priya and Wren held at the mill annex; Bea trades the final key's location for their release as police — tipped by the stream — arrive. Emotional beat: sacrifice paying out in people, not praise.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.summary: Trustees are arrested; the town's pension fraud becomes national news; Voss, cornered, implicates everyone including himself. Emotional beat: justice that feels both enormous and insufficient.

chapters.title: What the Keys Actually Open
chapters.summary: Ada Hollowmere reveals the vault's original purpose: a community endowment meant for the town, corrupted within a generation. Emotional beat: inheritance reunderstood.

chapters.title: The Semester That Wasn't Official
chapters.summary: Bea, facing expulsion for breaking into half the campus, is instead invited to help reform the trust's board — students included. Emotional beat: the outsider invited inside, on her terms.

chapters.title: Priya Comes Home
chapters.summary: Priya recovers at Bea's home; they argue, laugh, and read the ledger together, deciding what to keep secret and what to publish. Emotional beat: friendship repaired but changed.

chapters.title: Renewal
chapters.summary: A new, honest renewal ceremony: the keys returned to the town, the mill's endowment restored, Wren speaking first. Bea carries nothing this time. Emotional beat: tradition rebuilt as memory instead of debt.

chapters.title: The Unofficial Semester
chapters.summary: Bea's final narration: she keeps one key — the one that opens her father's unredacted file — and finally reads his last letter. She stops being careful and starts being free. Emotional beat: inheritance accepted, survival redefined.
